items.headline: Anthropic's stock closes its first day up 17%, valuing the Claude maker at about $1.76 trillion
items.summary: Shares of Anthropic (ticker ANT) closed Thursday at $97.17, about 17% above the $83 IPO price, after briefly trading as high as $111.50. That puts the company behind Claude at roughly $1.76 trillion on paper.
items.why_it_matters: Nothing changes in your Claude account today, but a cash-rich, publicly traded Anthropic is a strong sign Claude will keep getting investment and isn't going anywhere, which matters if you're building your business workflows on it.

items.headline: Claude Code adds an experimental 'Code Mode' that bundles several steps into one
items.summary: Claude Code, Anthropic's coding assistant that runs in a computer's terminal (the text-command window), has a new opt-in Code Mode that lets Claude write a small script to chain several actions together in one step instead of doing them one at a time. It's experimental and switched on with a settings flag.
items.why_it_matters: If you use Claude Code to build small tools or automations for your business, this may make multi-step jobs faster, but it's an early test, so beginners can safely wait until it becomes a regular feature.

items.headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a faster mid-tier model for paying Gemini users
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Neon, a new model that it says delivers near top-tier quality at faster speeds and lower cost. In the Gemini app it's available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, who pick it manually from the model menu; free users stay on the lighter models.
items.why_it_matters: If you already pay for Google AI Pro, you have a stronger option for long documents and analysis today, and it gives you a fair head-to-head against Claude before you decide which subscription is worth keeping.

items.headline: Gemini's Mac app can now click around your computer to finish tasks for you
items.summary: Google added 'computer use' to the Gemini desktop app for macOS, meaning Gemini can operate apps on your Mac to complete a task on your behalf. You can pause or stop it at any time and approve its actions before they happen.
items.why_it_matters: This is the same 'AI that does the clicking for you' idea Claude and ChatGPT are pushing, now from Google on the Mac, so if you're a Mac-based solo business owner it's another way to hand off boring admin chores, as long as you keep an eye on what it does.

categories.title: Tools & Tips for Creators and Small Biz

items.headline: Canva adds a single switch to turn off its AI features for Free and Pro accounts
items.summary: Canva is rolling out a setting that hides its generative AI tools, such as Magic Write, Magic Design, and Magic Expand, all in one place, plus a separate option to see fewer AI-made templates. AI stays on by default, and the rollout is gradual, so you may not see it yet.
items.why_it_matters: If AI buttons clutter your design workflow, or you want to promise clients that your graphics are made without AI, you can now control that yourself without upgrading to a team plan.

items.headline: Instagram's new Content Protection alerts you when someone reposts your Reels
items.summary: Instagram now scans for copies of a creator's original Reels and lets them block the repost or add a link back to the original. To qualify, the Reel must also be posted (or cross-posted) to Facebook, and a small group is testing detection of AI-altered copies that reuse the original audio.
items.why_it_matters: If you've ever found your videos reuploaded by someone else, this gives you a free way to get credit or shut it down, and turning on Facebook cross-posting is the simple step that makes your Reels eligible.

opportunity.action_note: Check Instagram's professional dashboard for Content Protection this week and turn on Facebook cross-posting for your Reels so new ones are covered.
opportunity.angle: Somebody stole my Reel, so I tested Instagram's new Content Protection tool

items.headline: TikTok begins rolling out Likeness Detection to help creators find AI deepfakes of themselves
items.summary: TikTok says it has started rolling out an opt-in Likeness Detection feature that, after you verify your identity, scans for AI-generated videos using your face so you can review and report them. It also launched a tool anyone can use to check whether a video is AI-generated.
items.why_it_matters: If you're the face of your brand, AI fakes of you selling something you never endorsed are a real risk, and this gives TikTok creators a way to catch them, similar to the likeness tool YouTube already offers.
